source.title: PairSAE: Mechanistic Interpretability from Pair Representations in Protein Co-Folding
source.authors: Giosue Migliorini; Aristofanis Rontogiannis; Grigori Guitchounts; Nicholas Franklin; Axel Elaldi; Olivia Viessmann

record.tranche_reason: It applies sparse-feature recovery to Boltz-2, a protein co-folding model, and reports how well recovered features align with biological annotations. This is an extension to a new model setting, not a test of toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition as background but does not test feature overlap, geometry, capacity pressure, or effects of sparsity or importance. The rows record its UniProt feature-annotation results. The LASSO affinity-prediction results concern downstream use of PairSAE features, not the recovery measure in V4.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs as a tool on Boltz-2, a protein co-folding model, not an LLM. Superposition is cited only as motivation. It reports its own method's performance: concept-probe F1 for PairSAE features against last-layer neurons of a different model (ESM2-650M). It never compares against Boltz-2's own neurons or tests overlap, capacity or feature geometry. The results therefore do not bear on whether real LLMs spread features across neurons or hold SAE-recoverable sparse features. They are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude PairSAE learns a shared feature basis across sequence and pair representations that encodes biophysically meaningful concepts and can generate hypotheses about Boltz-2 affinity predictions. Their stated limitation is that ligand-activating features were not mapped to concepts for lack of ligand annotations.
record.recipe_differences: This is a new sparse-autoencoder method for pairformer representations: it summarizes pair tensors with an N-mode SVD and decodes sequence and pair representations from shared features. It is not a reproduction of the toy-model method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper trains at layers 33 and 64; the reported concept-recovery percentages differ by layer and metric. The table labels the layer-33 model R3-L32, while the main text says R3-L33.

fits_no_version.finding: PairSAE features of Boltz-2 (16,384 latents, layers 33/64) give single-threshold probes with F1 ≥ 0.5 for 24–29% (token) and 50–53% (complex) of UniProt concepts. ESM2-650M last-layer neurons reach 0.8% and 19.7%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries on non-LLM biological foundation models (protein co-folding) recover features aligned with known biological annotations.

record.peer_reviewed: Machine Learning for Structural Biology Workshop, NeurIPS 2025
record.problems: The results concern one model family and two layers. The authors did not use MSA inputs and report that MSA-based affinity predictions differ substantially. Ligand-activating features could not be mapped to concepts because ligand annotations were limited. Table 1 has a layer-label discrepancy between R3-L32 and R3-L33. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the concept-recovery percentages.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 gives category-grouped concept counts, but the supplied text contains no readable numerical values for that breakdown. The LASSO affinity-prediction results and individual affinity-associated features were not extracted because they do not measure feature recovery or canonical model units.

untested.parts: All: toy-model overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity transition, geometry.
All: capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features.
No LLM is studied. No measure of feature spread across neurons. No Boltz-2 neuron baseline for SAE recovery.
Completeness, stability, canonicity of SAE features not tested.

missing.what: Per-category concept counts with F1 ≥ 0.5 (no readable numbers in the text)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T3/V4 'supports' label is rejected. The system is not an LLM. The neuron comparator comes from a different model (ESM2), so there is no within-model neuron-vs-SAE contrast. The probe picks the best of 16,384 features per concept, which inflates F1 relative to a neuron set of different size. Figure 1 values are cherry-picked examples. There are no controls or uncertainty estimates. The Table 1 label R3-L32 conflicts with the text's R3-L33.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity arises from competition for limited capacity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
The tested model is Boltz-2, not an LLM. The study does not measure feature spread across neurons or establish that SAE features are the model's complete feature set.
Completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features as units of the model.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

relation.reason: Superposition motivates the SAE approach; annotation probing and affinity prediction do not establish superposition or test dictionary completeness, stability or canonicality.

tranche.reason: Uses sparse dictionary learning to develop and evaluate PairSAE on protein co-folding representations; reports method performance without testing any listed claim version.

source_check.notes:
The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Rows are method comparisons or selected illustrations, not claim-testing evidence; none links to a listed version.
The R3-L32/R3-L33 discrepancy is in the source, and Figure 1 does not assign individual features to layers.
